guards.what: UNIT GAP: NondescriptGuilty's two card-reward screens are not modelled at all. Trial.cs:177-187 adds Doubt and then builds TWO `CardReward(CardCreationOptions.ForNonCombatWithDefaultOdds([Owner.Character.CardPool]), 3, Owner)` entries and hands them to RewardsCmd.OfferCustom; events/trial.py:90-93 adds Doubt and finishes, with a comment ('Two card-reward offers (RewardsCmd.OfferCustom) are not modelled') naming the omission
guards.issue: This is a MISSING EFFECT, wider than EV-4 (which is a modelled grant that should have been an offer) and wider than EV-6 (which is the wrong factory): here the screens, the cards and the draws are all absent. The sim has both halves of the capability -- rewards.create_reward_cards (rewards.py:235-275) is the faithful CreateForReward port for exactly the ForNonCombatWithDefaultOdds(characterPool) shape and events/brain_leech.py:44-47 already calls it, while Event.pending_reward_extras / resume_after_combat (events/base.py:94-99, 116-122) is the sim's take-or-skip channel -- so nothing was missing to build it with. EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/event_probes_b.py trialoffer`): driving the NONDESCRIPT page and choosing GUILTY raises ZERO card-selection screens and offers 0 cards where the game offers 2 screens x 3 = 6, and the deck delta is always exactly 1 (Doubt) where the game's is 1 to 3. LIVE: NONDESCRIPT is one of three equally weighted trials on an ungated event, and taking two card rewards is a large, permanent deck change. It also drops every draw CreateForReward would take off the Rewards stream, so the whole EV-6 observable set (rarity odds, the act-scaled upgrade draw, the stream) is absent rather than merely wrong.

guards.what: DoubleDown (Trial.cs:128-132) opens NAbandonRunConfirmPopup, whose Yes button calls RunManager.Instance.Abandon() (NAbandonRunConfirmPopup.cs:69-74); events/trial.py:63-65 calls run.kill() -- hp = 0 -- immediately and unconditionally
guards.rationale: Same observable outcome, different shape: the run is over either way, and for a headless sim 'abandoned' and 'dead' are the same terminal state. CRITICALLY, this is NOT an EV-1 site and must not be recorded as one (rule 3): EV-1's second verb is about run.kill standing in for `CreatureCmd.Kill(creature, force: false)`, whose Hook.ShouldDie / AfterPreventingDeath pass a belt Fairy in a Bottle answers. Abandon() is not CreatureCmd.Kill at all -- it is the meta run-teardown path the main menu and pause menu also use (NMainMenu / NPauseMenu / NAbandonRunButton are the other three callers), and CreatureCmd.cs:436 names 'abandoning a run' as precisely the `force: true` case that BYPASSES the pass. So no death-prevention listener would fire in the game either, and the sim loses nothing by not running one. Recorded here so a future reader does not add this to EV-1's site list by pattern-matching on run.kill.
